l4_steps.name: Receive IRROP alert from Operations Control Centre
l4_steps.input: OCC disruption notification (weather, ATC, mechanical, or crew IRROP)
l4_steps.output: IRROP event record opened in AMS with timestamp and flight reference
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS alert feeds from multiple upstream systems (NOC, Jeppesen, Altéa) with inconsistent data latency, causing duplicate or conflicting IRROP triggers during high-volume disruption events

l4_steps.name: Classify disruption type and assign severity tier
l4_steps.input: IRROP alert with reason code (WX, ATC, MX, CREW, OPS)
l4_steps.output: Severity tier (Tier 1: delay <2 hrs; Tier 2: delay 2–4 hrs; Tier 3: cancellation/diversion) logged in AMS
l4_steps.pain_point: Mechanical IRROPs often escalate from Tier 1 to Tier 3 mid-process due to late MX diagnosis; premature low-tier classification under-triggers rebooking resources

l4_steps.name: Confirm affected flight status in Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Flight number, departure date, disruption severity tier
l4_steps.output: Flight record locked for IRROP processing; passenger count confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Manifest retrieval time ≤2 min from alert
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS record locking conflicts when OCC and airport teams access the same flight simultaneously; requires coordinated queue management via PSS administrator role

l4_steps.name: Extract full passenger manifest for affected flight
l4_steps.input: Locked flight record in Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Full passenger manifest with PNR, contact details, connection itineraries, and ancillary services
l4_steps.kpi: Manifest extraction completeness 100% of checked-in and booked passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: Passengers booked via third-party OTAs often have incomplete contact data in Altéa, blocking automated notification and requiring manual agent outreach

l4_steps.name: Flag PRM, UM, and MAAS passengers requiring priority handling
l4_steps.input: Passenger manifest with SSR codes (WCHR, WCHC, UM, MAAS, MEDA)
l4_steps.output: Priority handling list dispatched to special assistance team and gate supervisor
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of SSR-flagged passengers identified before rebooking batch runs
l4_steps.pain_point: SSR codes entered by codeshare or interline partners are not always carried over into the operating carrier's Altéa record, creating missed-flag risk for vulnerable passengers

l4_steps.name: Determine EU261 / DOT compensation threshold applicability
l4_steps.input: Delay duration, disruption cause code, origin/destination jurisdiction, fare class
l4_steps.output: Compensation eligibility flag per passenger (EU261 / DOT Part 250 / no entitlement)
l4_steps.kpi: Eligibility determination completed before rebooking batch execution
l4_steps.pain_point: EU261 extraordinary-circumstances defence (e.g. ATC strike, severe weather) requires real-time legal review; automated rules engines in Altéa do not always capture all exemption nuances, exposing the airline to over- or under-payment

l4_steps.name: Execute automated mass rebooking via Altéa Inventory
l4_steps.input: Affected passenger manifest, compensation eligibility flags, available seat inventory on alternate flights
l4_steps.output: Automated rebooking records for ≥70% of affected passengers on next-available services
l4_steps.kpi: Auto-rebook success rate ≥70% of affected PAX; batch processing time ≤15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Inventory availability for the rebooking window is often constrained by already-high load factors (industry avg ≥83%), forcing passengers onto flights departing 24–48 hrs later and increasing duty-of-care cost

l4_steps.name: Identify and triage rebooking conflicts and seat oversells
l4_steps.input: Mass rebooking output; oversell alerts from Altéa Inventory
l4_steps.output: Conflict list with oversell count per flight, voluntary upgrade candidates, and interline options
l4_steps.kpi: Oversell resolution time ≤30 min; upgrade/interline acceptance rate ≥60%
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM inventory controls may auto-close cabin classes during the rebooking wave, preventing agents from placing passengers even when physical seats are available — requires temporary override authorisation from RM Analyst

l4_steps.name: Manually rebook complex and unresolvable itineraries
l4_steps.input: Conflict list from Step 3.2; interline partner availability via Sabre GDS or Travelport GDS
l4_steps.output: Confirmed alternate itinerary per complex passenger; interline endorsement where required
l4_steps.kpi: Manual rebook completion ≤60 min from conflict identification
l4_steps.pain_point: Interline rebooking requires bilateral interline agreements (IIAs); if the next-available flight is on a carrier with no IIA, agents must issue refunds rather than rebooking, increasing passenger dissatisfaction scores

l4_steps.name: Issue new boarding passes and update ancillary entitlements
l4_steps.input: Confirmed new itinerary records; pre-paid ancillaries (seat, bag, meal) on original booking
l4_steps.output: New boarding passes issued; ancillaries transferred or refund flag set
l4_steps.kpi: Boarding pass issuance ≤5 min per passenger post-rebooking confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: Ancillary transfer from disrupted to alternate flight is not fully automated in Altéa DCS; agents manually re-enter seat selections and meal preferences, adding ~3–4 min per PNR and creating ancillary revenue leakage

l4_steps.name: Trigger automated SMS and email notifications to affected PAX
l4_steps.input: Confirmed rebooking records; passenger contact data; disruption reason code
l4_steps.output: Outbound SMS/email sent to all passengers with new itinerary details and self-service rebooking link
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery rate ≥95% within 10 min of rebooking confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: Passengers with international mobile numbers often fail SMS delivery due to carrier routing gaps; email-only fallback is slower and has lower open rates during time-sensitive IRROP events

l4_steps.name: Update FIDS and gate display boards with disruption status
l4_steps.input: Disruption classification, new departure time or cancellation flag, alternate gate assignments
l4_steps.output: FIDS and gate display boards updated; PA announcement script generated for gate agents
l4_steps.kpi: FIDS update within 3 min of disruption classification confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS FIDS integration with some airport authority display networks requires manual refresh at certain stations, creating information lag of 5–15 min in secondary terminals

l4_steps.name: Brief gate agents and customer service desk on disruption status
l4_steps.input: Disruption ops log from AMS; rebooking summary from Altéa
l4_steps.output: Agent briefing completed; customer service desks staffed and equipped with voucher stock
l4_steps.kpi: Agent briefing completion ≤10 min from IRROP classification
l4_steps.pain_point: High-disruption events (weather cancellations affecting 20+ flights simultaneously) overwhelm customer service desk staffing ratios — airline contingency plans often require minimum 1:50 agent-to-passenger ratio, which is rarely met in mass IRROP scenarios

l4_steps.name: Assess duty-of-care entitlements by delay duration and cause
l4_steps.input: EU261/DOT eligibility flags from Step 2.3; confirmed delay/cancellation duration
l4_steps.output: Duty-of-care entitlement matrix per passenger (meals at 2 hrs, hotel at 4 hrs overnight, transport)
l4_steps.kpi: Entitlement assessment completed within 15 min of Tier 2/3 classification
l4_steps.pain_point: EU261 duty-of-care obligations apply regardless of extraordinary-circumstances defence — airlines frequently conflate compensation exemption with duty-of-care exemption, creating regulatory exposure under EC Regulation 261/2004 Art. 9

l4_steps.name: Issue meal and hotel vouchers to entitled passengers
l4_steps.input: Duty-of-care entitlement matrix; passenger count by entitlement tier
l4_steps.output: Meal and hotel vouchers issued; voucher serial numbers logged against PNR for cost recovery
l4_steps.kpi: Voucher issuance rate ≥90% of entitled passengers within 30 min of threshold trigger
l4_steps.pain_point: Many airlines operate VMS as a standalone system disconnected from Altéa PNR records; reconciling voucher costs against individual PNRs for EU261 cost recovery requires manual matching, creating audit gaps of up to 30% unreconciled spend

l4_steps.name: Manage passenger queue flow at rebooking and check-in desks
l4_steps.input: Volume of unreboooked passengers at gate; staffing plan from AMS resource module
l4_steps.output: Queue management plan activated; overflow desks opened; escalation to airport authority if required
l4_steps.kpi: Average passenger wait time at rebooking desk ≤20 min during IRROP event
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS resource scheduling module does not dynamically redeploy staff from non-disrupted gates during an IRROP event — staffing reallocation depends on supervisor radio coordination, adding 15–20 min to response time

l4_steps.name: Record disruption costs against flight and cost centre in SAP
l4_steps.input: Voucher serials, interline reissue charges, hotel invoices, overtime staffing costs
l4_steps.output: IRROP cost posting in SAP CO cost centre; accrual for EU261 claims liability
l4_steps.kpi: IRROP cost posting completed within 24 hrs of event closure
l4_steps.pain_point: Voucher costs from third-party hotel partners arrive as bulk invoices weekly, preventing real-time flight-level cost attribution in SAP CO and distorting disruption cost-per-passenger metrics

l4_steps.name: Submit EU261 / DOT compensation claims data to legal team
l4_steps.input: Eligibility flags, delay duration actuals, disruption reason code, passenger PNR list
l4_steps.output: Claims data package exported from Altéa; submitted to Legal and Customer Relations for processing
l4_steps.kpi: Claims data submitted within 48 hrs of event; EU261 response SLA ≤7 days per regulation
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO and IATA resolution frameworks for extraordinary-circumstances documentation are not standardised; each jurisdiction's CAA applies different evidence standards, requiring airline legal teams to maintain jurisdiction-specific defence packs

l4_steps.name: Generate IRROP performance report and update process KPIs
l4_steps.input: AMS event log, Altéa rebooking data, voucher costs, customer satisfaction (CSAT) scores
l4_steps.output: IRROP post-event report: rebooking rate, notification rate, avg wait time, duty-of-care compliance, cost-per-disrupted-passenger
l4_steps.kpi: Report published within 72 hrs; cost-per-disrupted-passenger target ≤$85 (industry benchmark)
l4_steps.pain_point: Data from SITA AMS, Altéa, VMS, and SAP sit in separate schemas with no native ETL integration; Tableau dashboards rely on nightly batch feeds, preventing real-time IRROP performance monitoring during the event itself
